summary: Democrat Amy Acton, the former state health director, faces Republican Vivek Ramaswamy for the open governor's seat, and Time reports a Marist poll released the week of October 21 showed Acton up seven points. The final stretch is dominated by a Ramaswamy ad featuring Acton's estranged mother that drew criticism from Gov. Mike DeWine and other Republicans, alongside a sharp contrast on taxes and data centers.

issues.why: Ramaswamy wants to phase out the state income tax starting with capital gains, while Acton opposes ending it and proposes a working families tax cut with child credits.
Ramaswamy would roll bills back to pre pandemic levels and cap growth, while Acton would expand the homestead exemption and offer rebates when bills jump more than 4 percent.
Acton backs a conditional moratorium and full utility cost recovery, while Ramaswamy wants them on old industrial sites generating their own power.
Both backed a state gas tax holiday that the Legislature passed in September as fuel prices climbed.
Ramaswamy supports executions for the worst cases while Acton would continue DeWine's moratorium.

storylines.title: Obama rallies for Acton in Cleveland
storylines.what: Acton focused on affordability at a Cleveland rally with Barack Obama and drew boos from the crowd when she criticized the ad featuring her mother.

storylines.title: Trump defends the ad, DeWine says pull it
storylines.what: Trump called the Ramaswamy ad very powerful and said he urged him to keep it up. DeWine said it is wrong and should come down but kept his endorsement.

storylines.title: Acton answers with counter ad
storylines.what: Acton's campaign released an ad featuring her brother, and the Columbus Dispatch endorsed Acton while condemning the Ramaswamy ad.

storylines.title: Dueling tax plans
storylines.what: Ramaswamy pitches eliminating the income tax and a property tax rollback, while Acton offers child credits and targeted property tax rebates. Neither campaign has fully explained how to pay for its plan.

storylines.title: Ramaswamy claims ad with Acton's mother
storylines.what: Ramaswamy confirmed his campaign made an ad in which Acton's estranged mother calls her a liar, saying it shows a pattern and that Acton will not debate him. Acton's campaign called it despicable.

storylines.title: Ramaswamy questions Acton's resume
storylines.what: Ramaswamy said Acton has not held a job longer than her stint as health director. Acton pointed to running a 1.6 billion dollar agency and said she faces over 100 million dollars in attack ads.

events.title: Income tax future
events.prompt: One plan would phase out Ohio's income tax over about a decade, which brings in billions a year. You are asked whether Ohio should go to zero.

opts.label: Working family credits
opts.say: Keep the income tax and add child and earned income credits for families under 85,000 dollars.

opts.label: Modest rate cut
opts.say: Trim rates gradually only as revenue allows.

opts.label: Go to zero
opts.say: Start with capital gains and phase out the income tax entirely, betting on growth.

events.title: Property tax relief
events.prompt: Homeowners saw bills jump after pandemic era revaluations. You must choose how to bring them relief.

opts.label: Fund schools fully
opts.say: Fully fund the school funding plan and expand the homestead exemption for seniors.

opts.label: Targeted rebates
opts.say: Send rebates of up to 1,000 dollars to households whose bills spike more than 4 percent.

opts.label: Roll back and cap
opts.say: Reset bills to 2021 levels and cap future growth.

events.title: The estranged mother ad
events.prompt: A 4 million dollar ad featuring the Democratic nominee's estranged mother is drawing criticism from both parties, and the governor has asked that it come down.

opts.label: Condemn and counter
opts.say: Call it a new low and answer with a family member's testimonial.

opts.label: Pull the ad
opts.say: Take the ad down and return to taxes and costs.

opts.label: Ride with it
opts.say: Keep the ad on air and say voters deserve to know.

events.title: Data center boom
events.prompt: Communities are fighting data centers over power and water. You must say whether Ohio should keep approving them.

opts.label: Conditional moratorium
opts.say: Pause new projects unless they cover all utility costs and use union labor.

opts.label: Brownfields only
opts.say: Steer them to old industrial sites with full property taxes and strict standards.

opts.label: Welcome investment
opts.say: Approve projects quickly to win jobs and tax base.

ads.theme: Acton's estranged mother calls her a liar, backed by a reported 4 million dollar buy.
Her brother responds to the Ramaswamy ad.

regions.name: Cleveland and Akron
regions.note: The Democratic base vote, anchored by Cleveland, with swingy collar suburbs.

regions.name: Columbus metro
regions.note: Fast growing and increasingly Democratic core with Republican leaning exurbs.

regions.name: Cincinnati and Dayton
regions.note: Hamilton County has turned blue while the surrounding suburbs remain strongly Republican.

regions.name: Mahoning Valley
regions.note: Old union steel country that swung hard to Trump.

regions.name: Northwest Ohio
regions.note: Toledo leans Democratic while farm counties to the south and west are deep red.

regions.note: Rural southeast that has become heavily Republican apart from Athens.
